title: Ordering at the mamak
blurb: Drinks first, then food — and what to do when the roti has run out.

notes.title: nak, tak, dah
notes.body: Three short forms carry most of this lesson: nak (hendak, want), tak (tidak, not) and dah (sudah, already). Nobody at a mamak says the long forms.

notes.title: Question with tak
notes.body: Put tak at the end to make a yes/no question: ada lagi tak? — is there still any (or not)?

notes.title: Item, then number
notes.body: The number comes after the thing: teh tarik satu, roti telur dua. Tweaks like kurang manis go last.

p1.en: What do you want to drink?
p1.note: nak = hendak. Staff often shorten it to just “Minum?”

p3.note: ada … tak? = is there … or not. lagi here means “still”.

p6.note: dulu = first / for now; it leaves the door open to add more later.

p7.note: kejap = sekejap. ye softens it, like “okay?”

p9.note: jugak = juga. A relaxed yes to a suggestion.

dialogue.en: What do you want to drink?
One teh tarik, less sweet.
Food?
One roti canai.
Is that all?
That's all for now. Thank you.

options: A teh tarik and one roti canai
Two teh tarik and no food
A roti canai and no drink
gist.why: Teh tarik satu … roti canai satu — one of each.

listen.en: What do you want to eat?
wrong: What do you want to drink?
Do you want to eat here?

listen.ms: Teh tarik dua, roti canai satu.
listen.en: Two teh tarik, one roti canai.

listen.ms: Teh tarik satu, roti canai dua. Itu je?
listen.en: One teh tarik, two roti canai. Is that all?

read.why: He asked about food, so name a dish.
You can turn food down: tak nak makan — just a drink.

dialogue.en: Yes, what do you want to drink?
One teh tarik, less sweet.
Food?
Is there still roti canai?

dialogue.ms: Roti canai dah habis lah. Roti telur ada.
dialogue.en: The roti canai's finished. There's roti telur.

dialogue.ms: Okay, roti telur satu lah. Kuah kari ye.
dialogue.en: Okay, one roti telur then. With curry gravy, please.
Is that all?
That's all for now. Thank you.
Okay, just a moment.

gist.q: What happened with the food order?
options: Roti canai was sold out, so she took roti telur
Roti telur was sold out, so she took roti canai
She skipped food and only had tea
gist.why: Roti canai dah habis … roti telur ada — so she switched to roti telur.

listen.ms: Roti telur dah habis. Roti canai ada lagi.
listen.en: Roti telur is finished. There's still roti canai.
wrong: Roti canai is finished. There's still roti telur.

listen.ms: Teh tarik dua. Satu kurang manis, satu biasa.
listen.en: Two teh tarik. One less sweet, one regular.
wrong: Two teh tarik, both less sweet.

listen.ms: Okay, roti canai dua lah. Kuah dhal ye.
listen.en: Okay, two roti canai then. With dhal, please.

listen.ms: Teh tarik kurang manis satu, roti telur satu. Itu je?
listen.en: One less-sweet teh tarik, one roti telur. Is that all?

read.right: Ada. Nak tambah teh tarik satu.
read.why: Yes, there is: ada, then say what to add.

read.prompt: Nasi goreng dah habis lah. Mee goreng ada.
read.why: He offered an alternative; take it with a soft lah.

read.en: The roti canai isn't finished yet.

dialogue.ms: Ya, duduk mana-mana pun boleh. Nak minum apa?
dialogue.en: Yes, sit anywhere you like. What do you want to drink?

dialogue.ms: Teh tarik satu, kurang manis. Kalau boleh, jangan manis sangat ye.
dialogue.en: One teh tarik, less sweet. If you can, not too sweet, okay.

dialogue.ms: Boleh, no problem. Makan apa hari ni?
dialogue.en: Sure, no problem. What are you eating today?

dialogue.ms: Roti canai ada lagi tak? Tadi nampak macam ramai orang.
dialogue.en: Is there still roti canai? It looked pretty busy just now.

dialogue.ms: Aduh, roti canai baru je habis. Kalau nak, kena tunggu lima belas minit macam tu.
dialogue.en: Ah, the roti canai just ran out. If you want it, you'll have to wait fifteen minutes or so.

dialogue.ms: Lama jugak tu. Roti telur ada tak?
dialogue.en: That's quite long. Is there roti telur?

dialogue.ms: Roti telur pun sama lah, semua roti kena tunggu. Maggi goreng ke, nasi goreng ke, cepat sikit.
dialogue.en: Roti telur's the same, all the roti need a wait. Maggi goreng or nasi goreng would be a bit quicker.

dialogue.ms: Okay lah, kalau macam tu bagi maggi goreng satu. Tak nak pedas sangat.
dialogue.en: Okay then, in that case give me one maggi goreng. Not too spicy.

dialogue.ms: Maggi goreng satu, kurang pedas. Telur mata nak tambah?
dialogue.en: One maggi goreng, less spicy. Want to add a fried egg?
Sure, why not. That's all for now.
Okay, done. Just a moment.

gist.q: Why did she end up with maggi goreng?
options: Every kind of roti needed a fifteen-minute wait
Maggi goreng was the cheapest thing
She changed her mind about the tea
gist.why: Semua roti kena tunggu — all the roti needed a wait, and he suggested something quicker.

listen.ms: Nasi goreng baru je habis. Kalau nak, kena tunggu sepuluh minit macam tu.
listen.en: The fried rice just ran out; about a ten-minute wait if you want it.
wrong: The fried rice will be ready in two minutes.
There's no more fried rice at all today.
The fried rice takes ten minutes; the noodles are finished.

listen.ms: Kalau macam tu, bagi nasi goreng satu. Pedas sikit takpe.
listen.en: In that case, give me one fried rice. A bit spicy is fine.

listen.ms: Semua roti ada, tapi maggi goreng kena tunggu sikit.
listen.en: All the roti are available, but the maggi goreng needs a short wait.
wrong: All the roti need a wait, but maggi goreng is quick.
Everything is finished except maggi goreng.
Roti and maggi goreng both need a long wait.

listen.ms: Lima belas minit lama jugak tu. Mee goreng ada tak?
listen.en: Fifteen minutes is quite long. Is there fried noodles?

listen.ms: Maggi goreng satu, tak nak pedas, tambah telur mata. Air teh tarik kurang manis kan?
listen.en: One maggi goreng, not spicy, add a fried egg. And the drink is a less-sweet teh tarik, right?

read.prompt: Roti kena tunggu lima belas minit. Okay ke?
read.right: Lama jugak tu. Maggi goreng cepat sikit tak?
read.why: Too long for you, so ask whether something else is quicker.

read.ms: Tak nak telur mata, itu je dulu.
read.en: No fried egg, that's all for now.

read.right: Tak payah lah, itu je dulu.
read.why: Turning down an extra: tak payah.

read.ms: Tadi nampak macam tak ramai orang.
read.en: It didn't look that busy just now.
